episode_title: 562: Does your website get you hired? with Alex Vita

real_qa.q: What signals indicate whether a photographer's website is actually helping them get hired?
real_qa.r: The easy answer is if it gets you inquiries and results for your business. But beyond analytics, you can ask clients how they found you through your contact form, and ask past clients what hesitations they had before reaching out. According to Alex Vita, these insights are often more valuable than analytics because they reveal what almost stopped prospects from contacting you.
real_qa.requete: how to know if website helps get hired

real_qa.q: What do first-time website visitors look for in a creative professional's portfolio within the first five seconds?
real_qa.r: First-time visitors, who represent about 90% of traffic, come with zero to negative trust, about five seconds of patience, and three competitor tabs open. They scan for what you do, who you work for, location if relevant, and what to do next. They also look for proof of work, a face, a price signal at least, and evidence of being human like a visible email or response time guarantee.
real_qa.requete: what do visitors look for on creative website first time

real_qa.q: Why do photographers' websites often fail to get them hired even when they showcase beautiful work?
real_qa.r: Many photographers have portfolio-only websites without clear positioning or audience in mind. Alex Vita explains that what makes a website work is clarity, proper copywriting, and curation—showing only the best work. A website is good when it has clear messaging about who you want to hire you and what transformation they get, not just beautiful photos. Too many creatives try to do too many jobs on the homepage, selling multiple services that don't work well together.
real_qa.requete: why photographer website not getting hired

real_qa.q: What is the difference between how repeat website visitors and first-time visitors behave on a creative's site?
real_qa.r: First-time visitors spend about five seconds making quick snap judgments where the homepage and hero section do the heavy lifting. Repeat visitors who already know you are looking to take a final decision or explore more deeply through portfolio pages, blog archives, and FAQ sections. For repeat visitors, copywriting depth, content expertise, and work quality matter most as they review examples and read detailed information.
real_qa.requete: repeat visitor vs first time visitor website behavior

real_qa.q: Should a creative professional build their own website or hire a designer, and what factors determine that decision?
real_qa.r: Building a website takes long because it involves two stacked projects: the technical part (templates, fonts, forms) which can be done in one to two weeks, and the strategy part (positioning, portfolio curation, copywriting) which is harder and often avoided. You should do it yourself only if budget is short or as a learning tool when your positioning is unclear. You should hire someone when your business is already working, you have clear positioning, and you need a revamp or design expertise.
real_qa.requete: should I build my own website or hire designer
